correctness.rationale: Grand CC/PAV scores follow from 2i+b=n and equality of interior/exterior edge counts for balanced vertex subsets. Every vertex-star group of d voters has one seat and worth d; sum of 2k groups requires aggregate payoff ≥n. Uniform edge payments equal to one achieve this lower bound and dominate any deviating coalition since score_R(e,T)≤number of approved selected vertices and Σ_{c∈T}deg_S(c)≤d|T|≤|S|. The difference n-v_R(E) is exactly the claimed CoS. Zero cost exactly bisection cuts all edges; positive-degree regular bipartite components have equal partition sizes. Exact verifier enumerated all labeled qualifying regular graphs of orders 2,4,6 (1+7+171) and full coalition constraints in seven examples. No unproved steps or numerical extrapolation.

value.rationale: The recent K4 TU CC/PAV nonexistence instance motivates precisely when cooperative stability can be bought and at what cost. The finding gives an exact graph invariant for an infinite natural incidence-election family, two scoring rules, a simple all-coalitions optimal allocation, and the bipartite yes/no boundary. It goes beyond the published finite obstruction or a routine score calculation; its structural bridge to maximum balanced cut may support graph-theoretic estimates and algorithms.
